Let me analyze the protocol carefully.

Key points:

1. Input: one JSON object on stdin with `directory`, `accounts`, `gateways`, `jobs`.
2. Output: `{"results":[...]}` in job order.

Directory: maps canonical identity (`sip:user@domain`, normalized) to array of aliases (normalized sip or tel URIs, ≤256 chars). Canonical identity itself is always an alias. Aliases belong to exactly one canonical identity.

Accounts: maps arbitrary subject string to `{"primary":identity,"allow":[identity,...]}`. Primary implicitly allowed. Every account identity is a directory key.

Gateways: maps gateway name to `{"local_domains":[domain,...],"peers":{name:[domain,...]}}`.

Job: `gateway`, `ingress`, `trusted_out` (bool), and exactly one of `raw` or `source` (earlier job index).

If source job rejected → reject with `upstream`.

Ingress: `{"kind":"local","subject":s}`, `{"kind":"peer","name":p}`, `{"kind":"untrusted"}`.

Limits: request text longer than 32768 chars → `syntax`.

SIP framing:
- First CRLF CRLF divides header section and body.
- Header-section line ends with CRLF only: bare LF or CR, missing terminator, non-ASCII, or controls other than HTAB → syntax errors.
- Body may contain ASCII printable chars, HTAB, CR, LF; all other controls, DEL, non-ASCII anywhere → syntax errors.
- Request line: `METHOD SP URI SP SIP/2.0` with exactly two single spaces. METHOD is case-sensitive INVITE or MESSAGE.
- At most 512 physical header lines and 128 logical header fields.
- Line beginning SP/HTAB continues preceding field: replace the line break and maximal leading SP/HTAB run with one SP. Orphan continuation invalid.
- New header: nonempty token name, optional SP/HTAB, colon, value.
- Token chars: ASCII letters/digits and `- . ! % * _ + ` ' ~` (backtick between plus and apostrophe is a token char).
- Strip outer SP/HTAB from values after unfolding.
- Names case-insensitive. Compact: f→From, t→To, i→Call-ID, l→Content-Length, c→Content-Type.
- Exactly one each of From, To, Call-ID, CSeq, Content-Length required.
- At most one each of P-Preferred-Identity, Remote-Party-ID, Privacy, Content-Type.
- P-Asserted-Identity may repeat; concatenate address lists in arrival order.
- Other fields may repeat, discarded.
- Missing/duplicate required or optional singleton → syntax.

- Call-ID matches `[A-Za-z0-9_.@+-]{1,128}`.
- CSeq: decimal digits, one or more SP/HTAB, and the exact request method; number in 1..2147483647.
- Content-Length: nonempty decimal digits (leading zeros permitted), must equal ASCII body length exactly.
- Content-Type: if present, nonempty sequence of printable ASCII and HTAB; retain unfolded, outer-trimmed value verbatim.
- Privacy: `id` or `none`, case-insensitive.

Address grammar:
- From and To contain exactly one address, with optional `;tag=TOKEN` afterward.
- Allow SP/HTAB around semicolon and equals, and around the tag value.
- Tag is case-sensitive, 1-128 token chars; param name case-insensitive.
- No other header params supported.
- PPI, RPID, PAI addresses have no header parameters.
- PPI and RPID contain exactly one address.
- Total PAI addresses must be 1 or 2; if 2, exactly one sip and the other tel.
- Address is bare URI, or `[DISPLAY SP/HTAB] <URI>` (whitespace before `<` optional, DISPLAY optional). Allow SP/HTAB immediately inside `<` and `>`.
- Display name: one or more tokens separated by SP/HTAB, or a quoted string. In a quoted string, backslash escapes exactly the next printable ASCII char or HTAB. Unescaped double quote closes string. Angle brackets, commas, semicolons inside quoted strings are data.
- Display name never identifies sender. Unterminated quotes, dangling escapes, nested angle brackets, stray text, empty addresses → syntax.
- Commas separate PAI addresses only outside quoted strings and angle brackets; no empty list members.

URI:
- sip URI: `sip:USER@HOST`, case-insensitive scheme. USER: nonempty sequence of ASCII letters/digits and `- _ . ! ~ * ' ( ) +` or `%HH` escapes. Each escape must decode to one of those permitted USER characters. Decode exactly once. USER case-sensitive.
- HOST: DNS name: one or more dot-separated labels of 1-63 letters/digits/hyphens, each beginning and ending in letter/digit; max 253 chars before optional single trailing dot. Lowercase HOST and remove optional trailing dot. Escapes in HOST forbidden.
- No ports, URI params, passwords, query, IPv4/IPv6-specific syntax, sips scheme.
- Numeric DNS label allowed.
- tel URI: `tel:+DIGITS` case-insensitive scheme, 1-15 decimal digits, first nonzero.
- No whitespace inside URI.
- From, To, PPI, RPID, PAI may use either scheme; request-line URI must use sip.
- Canonical To and request URI use lexical normalization only.
- Preserve validated From and To tags.
- `sip:anonymous@anonymous.invalid` reserved, never a directory alias, valid only as From or To value (or request URI). Using in PPI/PAI/RPID is syntax. It is the sole anonymous From representation.

Identity policy:
- Validate the entire request grammar first, including identity headers to be stripped. Syntax failures take precedence over authentication/identity failures.
- No claim inferred from body or ignored headers.

Local:
- Subject must exist. Every nonanonymous From and any PPI must resolve to an allowed account identity whose canonical domain is hosted by this gateway. Select PPI if present, otherwise nonanonymous From, otherwise account primary. The selected identity must also be hosted and allowed.
- PAI and RPID from local endpoint convey no authority, ignored after syntax validation.

Peer:
- Peer must be listed and PAI must exist. All PAI claims must resolve to the same identity, within a domain in this peer's authority list. Every nonanonymous From, any PPI and any RPID must resolve to that same identity. Anonymous From allowed. Select that asserted identity.

Untrusted: reject (unauthenticated).

- Unknown local subjects, unknown peers, untrusted ingress, listed peer with no PAI → `unauthenticated`.
- Otherwise any failed lookup, authorization, hosting, peer authority, or identity agreement → `identity`.

- A listed peer's authority can include a locally hosted domain; a gateway's own local_domains never implicitly grant authority to its peers.
- URI aliases may resolve to the same identity despite differing schemes, users or hosts.

Privacy:
- Privacy active if From is anonymous OR Privacy is `id`.
- On acceptance, return selected canonical identity for audit, rewrite From to that identity, or to reserved anonymous URI when private.
- Emit a single canonical PAI with selected identity if privacy inactive OR trusted_out is true; otherwise omit PAI.
- Always conceal From when private.
- PPI, RPID, original display-names, original PAI, Authorization, Contact, Via and all other unlisted fields never survive normalization.

Output format:
```
METHOD normalized-request-URI SIP/2.0
From: <selected-or-anonymous-URI>[;tag=from-tag]
To: <normalized-To-URI>[;tag=to-tag]
Call-ID: original-call-id
CSeq: numeric-value-without-leading-zeros METHOD
Privacy: id-or-none
P-Asserted-Identity: <selected-URI>          (only when emitted)
Content-Type: original-normalized-value    (only when present)
Content-Length: decimal-body-length
```
Follow last header with CRLF CRLF then original body, no added trailing line ending.

### Address parsing implementation

```
def parse_address(value, pos, allow_tag):
    # returns (uri_normalized, tag_or_None, newpos)
    start = pos
    # skip leading whitespace
    while pos < len(value) and value[pos] in ' \t': pos += 1
    if pos >= len(value): error
    c = value[pos]
    if c == '"':
        pos = parse_quoted(value, pos)  # display
        # skip whitespace
        while pos < len(value) and value[pos] in ' \t': pos += 1
        if pos >= len(value) or value[pos] != '<': error
        uri, pos = parse_bracketed(value, pos)
    elif c == '<':
        uri, pos = parse_bracketed(value, pos)
    else:
        # check for scheme prefix
        if value[pos:pos+4].lower() == 'sip:' or value[pos:pos+4].lower() == 'tel:':
            uri, pos = parse_bare_uri(value, pos)
        else:
            # display name: tokens separated by whitespace
            pos = parse_display_tokens(value, pos)
            while pos < len(value) and value[pos] in ' \t': pos += 1
            if pos >= len(value) or value[pos] != '<': error
            uri, pos = parse_bracketed(value, pos)
    # tag param
    tag = None
    p = pos
    while p < len(value) and value[p] in ' \t': p += 1
    if p < len(value):
        if value[p] != ';': error
        p += 1
        while p < len(value) and value[p] in ' \t': p += 1
        # param name
        m = re.match(r'[tokenchars]+', value[p:])
        if not m: error
        name = m.group(0)
        p += len(name)
        if name.lower() != 'tag': error
        while p < len(value) and value[p] in ' \t': p += 1
        if p >= len(value) or value[p] != '=': error
        p += 1
        while p < len(value) and value[p] in ' \t': p += 1
        # tag value: token chars, 1..128
        m = re.match(r'[tokenchars]+', value[p:])
        if not m: error
        tagval = m.group(0)
        if len(tagval) > 128: error
        tag = tagval
        p += len(tagval)
        pos = p
    return uri, tag, pos
```
